title: Selector law as product retention
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite type, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $\theta\in[-1,1]$. The joint distribution formed by drawing two independent values from $\pi$ and selecting between them using a correlated sign pair with parameter $\theta$ equals the joint distribution formed by drawing the first value from $\pi$ and, for the second coordinate, retaining it with probability $(1+\theta)/2$ and otherwise drawing independently from $\pi$.
